failure_modes.message: newcomer was not admitted as a validator on all nodes under chaos (V1: a precommit is missing)
failure_modes.what_happened: These counts come from the 7 traced failures; all 17 untraced failures in the 800-run measurement had the same message. In these 3, the other three nodes decided a height (1, 1 and 4) and moved on. The stuck node held that height's proposal, all 4 prevotes, and only its own precommit plus one other: 2 of the 3 it needed (quorum 267 of 400). chaosNet had dropped every copy of the 2 missing precommits, both direct sends and relays. Relays stop once a node decides, so no more copies were coming. With no quorum of any precommits, the node never armed the precommit timeout and sat at round 0 for the rest of the run. The others spent about 100 ms at the next height, between two 400 ms re-gossip ticks. The ticks fire at the same moment on all four nodes because they all start together. So the 9697404 re-gossip of the last commit never reached the stuck node.

failure_modes.message: newcomer was not admitted as a validator on all nodes under chaos (V2: the proposal is missing)
failure_modes.what_happened: The stuck node, at heights 1, 3, 4 and 5, missed all 3 copies of the deciding round-0 proposal: the proposer's send and two relays, every one dropped (shown in the drop log). It received a quorum of precommits for that block. The quorum of precommits armed the precommit timeout, so it timed out and moved to round 1, where it waited for good. This is the earlier diagnosis of 'stuck at round 1' in a more precise form: in every round-1 case the precommits were there and only the block was missing. Nothing at HEAD ever re-sends a decided proposal: commit() clears heightProposals, reGossipProposal sends only the current round's proposal at the current height, and relay happens only on first receipt. A later problem made it worse in most dumps. The test keeps paying 21 from node 0 to the newcomer, which has no node, until every node has admitted it. With one node stuck, 2 or more payments landed. The three running nodes were then left with 257 of 399 power, below the quorum of 267. They froze at about height 7 with 3 nil prevotes and no precommits. This came after the failure and did not cause it.

investigations.root_cause:
The other three nodes decide a height without one node, which has lost every copy of one decisive message: a precommit it needs, or the proposal. That node holds everything else and cannot decide. Two things fail to recover it.

First, at 35b4e7f a decided proposal is never re-sent. commit() resets heightProposals, reGossipProposal sends only heightProposals[driver.Round()] at the current height, and relay fires only on first receipt at the current height.

Second, the last commit's precommits (9697404) go out only on the re-gossip tick, every cfg.Timeout (400 ms in the test, 3 s in production), and only while the next height's driver runs. In the test the next height took about 100 ms, and the ticks are in phase on all nodes. The others passed through it between ticks, after which no node held that height any more.

So the node needed a checkpoint. chaosNet serves none, so it stayed stuck. Production has the same gap: catchUpSources polls only the configured bootstrap peers when there are any, so a node whose bootstrap peers are down stays behind for good. If its vote is needed, the network halts at the next height, and the re-gossip there sends precommits but never the block.

Fix: commit() keeps the decided proposal (lastProposal) and immediately broadcasts it together with the commit's precommits (gossipLastCommit). Every re-gossip tick sends both again. A node already past that height drops them on its height checks.

No Go 1.27 effect: 6/200 under go1.27.3 and 6/200 under go1.26.4. The stall needs only lost messages and the tick phase. The node's timers are AfterFunc, which the asynctimerchan setting does not affect.

fixes.summary: chaos: send a height's decision as it commits, to a node still deciding it. New field Node.lastProposal is set in commit() from heightProposals[act.Round]. New helper gossipLastCommit broadcasts lastCommit.Votes and also lastProposal when lastProposal.Height == lastCommit.Height > 0. It is called at the end of commit() and from reGossipVotes, replacing that function's old loop over the last commit's votes. Production code grows by about 10 lines plus comments. Regression test TestTheCommitCarriesTheDecisionToANodeStillAtThatHeight: one node decides height 1. A second node, holding every prevote but not the proposal, is fed only what the first sent from its decisive precommits onward. It must then decide.
fixes.fails_without_fix: Yes, checked in the scratch copy, by restoring 35b4e7f's node.go (and the same once in the worktree, restored straight after): window_test.go:254 'the node still at height 1 did not decide from what the deciding node sent as it committed'. It also fails with either half of the fix removed: without the commit-time send, and without the proposal in the decision. A first draft that only added the proposal to the periodic re-gossip passed the deterministic test but left V1 (missing precommits) untouched, which is why the commit-time send was added.

investigations.doubts:
1. The GODEBUG=asynctimerchan=1 comparison cannot be run as asked: go1.27.3 aborts with 'fatal error: removed GODEBUG "asynctimerchan" set to old value "1"'. To separate a runtime effect from a GODEBUG effect I used two other configurations instead: go1.27.3 with the go 1.22 line, and go1.26.4 with asynctimerchan=0. go126sync's 1/200 against 6/200 is not significant (Fisher p ≈ 0.12).
2. Load was not controlled. The before batches ran at load average 3.6-11, with my instrumented runs and other agents' chaos tests running alongside. That probably explains 6/200 against the earlier 298/300 for the same go1.26.4 configuration. The after batches ran under more load (6.3-16), so the drop to zero is not a load artifact.
3. A residual gap remains. A node two or more heights behind still needs a checkpoint, and chaosNet has none. It was not seen in 1,400 runs after the fix.
4. A separate production gap is not fixed here. catchUpSources never falls back to the gossip peers when bootstrap peers are configured, so a node whose bootstrap peers are dead and which falls 2 or more heights behind never catches up. The fix would be small: poll bootstrap plus transport peers. It is out of scope for this test.
5. Cost of the fix: every commit now re-sends the decided block once to all peers, and again on each re-gossip tick while the next height runs. That roughly doubles proposal traffic. Nodes already past that height drop it on the first height check.
6. The test is unchanged, because its assertion is something the protocol promises. Two things about it are worth knowing. Its comment says there is no phantom validator, but the newcomer has no running node once it is admitted. Its retry loop keeps moving node 0's stake to the newcomer while any node lags, which turns one stuck node into a network halt.

failure_modes.message: the equivocating validator was not slashed out on all honest nodes (R1: precommit lost at the slashing height)
failure_modes.what_happened: Traced at 35b4e7f: 1 of 600 runs at 10% loss, and 9 of the 15 failures at 30% loss. At height 2, the height whose block slashes the double-signer, one honest precommit was dropped on all three paths to one node (the direct send and both relays). With the double-signer counted out, that node needs all 4 honest precommits. The others decided, and at height 3 the double-signer was gone, so 3 of 4 was a quorum and they did not wait. The last commit reaches a node still at height 2 only through re-gossip, every 400 ms. All nodes start together, so their ticks fall at the same moments. The others finished height 3 in about 150 ms, between two ticks, and from then on re-gossiped later commits. The node stayed at height 2 for good. Example trace: <scratch>/eqv/logs/diag-head/fail-1793118681568134680.txt (n3's height-2 round-1 precommit was dropped toward n1 by n3, n2 and n0; the others committed h2 at about 2105 ms and h3 at about 2221-2262 ms; the ticks came at about 2000 ms and 2401 ms).

failure_modes.message: the equivocating validator was not slashed out on all honest nodes (R2: decided on the double-signer's vote before precommitting)
failure_modes.what_happened: Traced: 5 of the 15 failures at 35b4e7f at 30% loss, 1 at 20% loss, and 1 of 6 at 8f4b3cb at 10% loss. One node got the double-signer's precommit for the block before its conflicting one, plus three honest precommits, and decided before it had a prevote quorum, so it never precommitted. The other honest nodes had seen both of the double-signer's precommits, so VoteSet counts it out. While it is in the set they need all 4 honest precommits, and the decider's never existed. The commit the decider re-gossips has the same 3 honest votes plus the double-signer's. The decider waited at the next height for them, so the whole network halted. Example: <scratch>/eqv/logs/diag-c99/fail-1793118304923972207.txt (n2 decided at 311 ms with byz,n0,n1,n3 and had only n1,n2,n3 prevotes).

failure_modes.message: the equivocating validator was not slashed out on all honest nodes (R2': same, but a fourth honest node precommitted nil; NOT fixed)
failure_modes.what_happened: 1 of the 15 failures at 35b4e7f at 30% loss, and all 3 of the 300 runs that failed with the fix at 30% loss. Never seen at the test's 10% loss. The decider precommitted the block, but its quorum counted the double-signer, and the fourth honest node precommitted nil in that round after its prevote timeout. The nodes that count the double-signer out hold 3 honest precommits for the block. They can never get a fourth, because the decider has moved to the next height. Only a checkpoint catch-up resolves this.

failure_modes.message: the equivocating validator was not slashed out on all honest nodes (M1 at 8f4b3cb, fixed by 9697404)
failure_modes.what_happened: 4 of 6 traced failures at 8f4b3cb. Before the slash, an honest precommit was dropped on all three paths to one node. The deciders moved to the next height. There they still needed that node, but nobody ever re-sent the precommit, so all nodes waited for good. 9697404 (re-gossip of lastCommit.Votes while the next height runs) fixes this: bf7c886 failed 5/200 and 9697404 0/200 under go1.27.3. TestReGossipCarriesTheLastCommitToANodeStillAtThatHeight fails at head if that loop is removed.

failure_modes.message: network stopped committing after the slash
failure_modes.what_happened: Not reproduced at 8f4b3cb, 6ad9e3b, bf7c886, 9697404, 35b4e7f or with the fix: 0 in more than 2,000 untraced and 1,000 traced runs. Reproduced at 9a60643, 2 of 123 traced runs. Mechanism is E14. A precommit timeout armed at an earlier height fired into the next height's driver and moved one of the three post-slash nodes to round 1 before it precommitted in round 0, so the nodes split across rounds and none reached a quorum. Meanwhile the fourth node sat a height behind, because the old driver had taken its proposal in the post-commit window. 4a7fa73 (E14, before 8f4b3cb) fixed this by scoping timers to their height and holding window proposals. Detector output: <scratch>/eqv/scripts/stale9a6.py found such a timer in 4 of the 5 failures at 9a60643, including both of these.

investigations.root_cause:
Before the slash commits, the network has no spare votes. There are 4 honest validators plus the double-signer, each with power 100, and the quorum is 334. Every node that has seen both of the double-signer's conflicting votes counts it out, so it needs all 4 honest votes. chaosNet has no checkpoint catch-up source, so a node left at a height without what it needs to finish it stays there for good.

The test has failed this way for three different reasons over time:
1) At 9a60643: E14 stale timers and post-commit-window proposals, which caused both failure messages. Fixed by 4a7fa73.
2) At 8f4b3cb: about 5%, with no Go-version effect (10/200 under go1.27.3, 6/200 under go1.26.4). Mostly an honest precommit lost on every path to one node while the deciders, still needing it, never re-sent it. Fixed by 9697404: bf7c886 5/200, 9697404 0/200.
3) At 35b4e7f it still fails, 1/400 under go1.27.3 and 1/200 under go1.26.4. There are two production liveness gaps:
   - R1: at the slashing height, the others stop needing the straggler at the next height. They pass that height before their in-phase 400 ms re-gossip, so the straggler never gets the commit.
   - R2: a node decides on a quorum that counted the double-signer's vote, before it has precommitted itself. The nodes that counted the double-signer out can never complete that quorum.

In production, both gaps are repaired by checkpoint catch-up within one poll (at least 3 s), and the whole network waits during that time before the slash. A node whose bootstrap peers are dead never recovers, because catchUpSources then returns only those peers.

E35 is why the decider in R2 still records the evidence, from the late conflicting precommit, so the slash proceeds. E13 matters because in static mode the slashed key keeps its seat, so R2 is possible at every height, not just until the slash.

A third case remains: R2', where the decider did precommit but a fourth honest node precommitted nil. It cannot be fixed with honest votes alone.

fixes.summary: chaos: precommit the block a node decides before it has precommitted. When the driver decides a round it has not precommitted in (sentPrecommit false), it first casts its precommit for the decided block, so the commit it hands on carries an honest vote that the nodes counting the double-signer out can use. The block is already decided, so the vote cannot complete any other quorum. The vote goes through castVote and the sign log as usual.

investigations.doubts:
1) R2' is not fixed. It appeared 1/300 at 35b4e7f and 3/300 with the fix at 30% loss, and never at the test's 10% loss. A node decides on a quorum that counted the double-signer, and a fourth honest node had precommitted nil, so the nodes that count the double-signer out hold 3 of the 4 honest votes they need. Two ways to close it, both the owner's call:
   - Count a double-signer's precommit when it is part of a commit for the block. Commit.Verify, and so checkpoint catch-up, already does this. It contradicts docs/consensus.md ('a double-signer cannot help form a quorum') and the burn principle.
   - Rely on catch-up, which chaosNet lacks.

2) catchUpSources returns only the bootstrap peers when any are configured. A node whose bootstrap peers are dead therefore never falls back to its gossip peers, and never recovers from R2' or from a height it lacks the block for. Before the slash, the whole network waits on such a node. A one-line fallback would fix it; I left it alone because the test never takes that path.

3) A node that lacks the decided block of its own height has no gossip recovery once its peers move on, because nobody re-sends the decided proposal. I did not see this in this test at head. It is the 'stuck without the proposal' mode reported for TestChaosDynamicAdmissionConverges, and that agent may also be editing reGossipVotes or commit, so a merge may conflict with 01f0f34.

4) At the test's own 10% loss the improvement is not statistically shown: 2/800 before, 0/600 after, across toolchains. The evidence is the traced 30%-loss runs (R1 and R2 went from 14 of 300 to 0) and the deterministic tests.

5) Traced runs log every event, which slows the -race event loop, so the mix of failure modes in traced runs may differ from untraced runs.

6) GODEBUG=asynctimerchan=1 makes go1.27.3 abort ('removed GODEBUG asynctimerchan set to old value'). The runtime/GODEBUG split therefore used go1.26.4 with a go 1.26 line instead. No Go 1.27 effect showed: 8f4b3cb failed 10/200 under go1.27.3 and 6/200 under go1.26.4, and 35b4e7f failed 1/400, 1/200 and 0/200 across the three setups.

7) Each node now broadcasts the last commit once more per height (N small votes). Receivers already past that height drop them with a digest comparison before any signature check.

8) The driver now signs a precommit after it already holds a precommit quorum. I argued this is safe: the vote is for the decided block, in a round the node never precommitted in, and goes through the sign log. Still, it changes the protocol and deserves review.

9) post-emudhra-phase1 moved to 7024176 while I worked. I did not touch it, and this branch sits on 35b4e7f.

investigations.root_cause:
A validator is left one height behind and never recovers, because after a height is decided nothing re-sends that height's proposal.

Code path:
- A proposal is broadcast once by the proposer and relayed once by each node that takes it (onProposal, then relay).
- reGossipProposal re-sends only the driver's current round at the current height.
- Three of four validators are a quorum and decide in about 100 ms, before the first 400 ms re-gossip tick. From then on the decided proposal is never sent again.
- A precommit is relayed only by nodes still at that height (countable), so a late precommit has a single path.
- The commit's precommits (reGossipVotes, lastCommit.Votes) went out without the proposal, and only on the 400 ms tick. By then the others, at about 6 blocks/s, had usually moved past the next height and were sending a later commit.

The driver decides only when it holds the proposal of the precommit round. In 10 traced strandings, 5 nodes held a 2/3 precommit quorum but no proposal and 5 held the proposal one precommit short. Their propose and precommit timers kept moving them to new rounds that could never decide. A node keeps no blocks, so only a checkpoint from catchUpLoop (every 3 s) can free it. chaosNet has no catch-up source. Neither has a production node whose bootstrap peers are dead, because catchUpSources returns only the configured bootstrap peers whenever any are set.

Scratch end-to-end reproduction (<scratch>/lossdup/repro/zz_halt_repro_test.go): one validator down after height 1, plus one validator with a dead bootstrap peer that lost every copy of the height-1 proposal. On HEAD the 4-validator network halts at height 2 for good (3/3 runs). With the fix it resumes in 0.55 s.

Mechanism evidence from instrumented runs (<scratch>/lossdup/diag), 80 runs each:
- baseline: 10 stranded, 2 failed
- re-sending on the tick only: 7 stranded, 1 failed (not enough)
- re-sending at commit and on the tick: 0 stranded, 0 failed

Progress threshold: the test asks for 6 blocks in 4 s. That is not stronger than what the protocol delivers at its timeouts with four live validators: at least 16 blocks in all 1140 unstranded runs before the fix, at least 18 in 1000 runs after. Only runs with a stranded validator fell to 3-10. The test is unchanged.

Go version: go1.27.3 does not fail more often. Before the fix the shipped config failed 3/400 and the old setup 7/300, and every configuration stranded a validator in 10-12% of runs. The earlier 2/22 against 0/20 was noise. The requested split cannot be run as asked, because GODEBUG=asynctimerchan=1 is fatal on go1.27.3. fixes.summary: In node/node.go, commit() now keeps the decided proposal (lastProposal = heightProposals[act.Round]) and calls the new sendLastCommit(). sendLastCommit broadcasts lastCommit.Votes and that proposal (only when its height equals lastCommit's, so stale or zero values are never sent). reGossipVotes now calls sendLastCommit instead of sending lastCommit.Votes itself. A validator still at the decided height therefore gets the full certificate as the others commit, while it is at most one height behind, and again on every re-gossip tick. Production change: about 20 lines including comments. The regression test TestTheLastCommitCarriesItsProposal is in node/window_test.go; it is deterministic, uses handNet and needs no timers.

investigations.doubts:
How the numbers were measured: compiled race test binaries (go test -c -race) run directly with -test.count=10 per batch, which is equivalent to -p 1 on one package. The scratch copies had one added t.Logf line (PROGRESS heights) so stranding could be counted; it is not committed and does not change pass or fail. With failures at about 1-2%, the before/after contrast in failures alone is modest (3/400 against 0/400 for the shipped config). The strong signal is stranding: 137/1300 against 0/1000. An early sign that the old setup stranded less (1/68) disappeared with more data (28/300).

The task's premise about GODEBUG is wrong for this toolchain: GODEBUG=asynctimerchan=1 under go1.27.3 is fatal at startup, not a way back to async timers. Any earlier run made with it did not execute tests.

Cost of the fix: each node now re-sends the decided block once per commit and once per re-gossip tick, plus a quorum of precommits at commit. In this 4-node setup that roughly doubles proposal sends per height. Receivers drop the copies cheaply, but large blocks cost bandwidth. The cheaper tick-only variant was measured as not enough (7/80 stranded against 10/80). With production timing (3 s tick, about 1 s blocks), only the send at commit reaches a node that is one height behind in time.

Not fixed, separate production gap: a node more than one height behind still needs a checkpoint. catchUpSources ignores live gossip peers whenever bootstrap peers are configured, so a node whose bootstrap peers are dead never catches up. It is not on this test's path, because chaosNet has no catch-up source at all.

TestChaosDynamicAdmissionConverges (another agent's test) strands the same way, and this fix took it from 9/300 to 0/300 in my cross-check; its owner should confirm.

problems.detail: The investigator's before and after measurements were not interleaved with each other: before ran 16:11-16:38 and after ran 16:40-16:50, interleaved only across toolchain configurations. Their 6/200 against 0/200 alone gives only p = 0.03. The pre-fix rate also varies a lot over time. My uninstrumented pre-fix side had 3 of its 8 failures in its first 100 runs and then 0 in 400, while the instrumented stream failed 10/440 in the same window. Passing-run durations were identical (0.66-0.68 s), so this is noise and load, not the instrumentation. My ABBA data (8/1000 against 0/1000, p = 0.008) settles it.

The cost note understates the extra traffic. At every commit, every node now re-sends every precommit in the commit to all peers, not only the block: about N x |commit| x (N-1) extra vote messages per height across the network, O(N^3). Before the fix that burst went out only on re-gossip ticks during the next height. It is negligible at 4 validators but worth stating for large validator sets.

The new regression test pins one stuck state: round 0, no proposal, no precommits held. It does not pin the two states actually seen in failures: V1 (proposal, all prevotes, 2 of 3 precommits) and V2 (round 1 after timeouts, precommit quorum, no proposal). My scratch tests show the fix resolves both and the reverted code resolves neither, so this is a coverage gap, not a defect.

The 'production bug' label is narrower than stated. Without Bootstrap configured, catchUpSources falls back to the gossip peers (HTTPTransport.Peers). A production node stuck in V1 or V2 then catches up from a checkpoint within max(3 s, 5 x MinBlockInterval). The stall is permanent only when bootstrap peers are configured but unreachable, or when there is no checkpoint source, as in chaosNet. The fix still removes that stall and the halt at the next height when the stuck node's vote is needed.

Two residual gaps remain; neither was observed in 1,500 runs with the fix. (a) A node 2 or more heights behind still needs a checkpoint. (b) Suppose the decision came at round R, more than one round past the stuck node's round, and the proposal copy arrives before the precommits that trigger the round skip; HTTP Broadcast posts each message in its own goroutine and chaosNet randomizes delay, so this can happen. onProposal then drops it (p.Round > round()+1), and the next copy comes only with a re-gossip tick during the next height.

verifications.notes:
The root cause and the fix both hold up.

**Rates (check 1):** the pre-fix side failed 8/1000 and the fix side 0/1000, in ABBA-interleaved batches under the required configuration. The instrumented ABBA stream gave 6/500 against 0/500. The fix side showed no failure, panic or data race in any stream.

**Root cause, confirmed with my own instrumentation:** I added a node-state dump on failure to scratch copies only. All 16 instrumented pre-fix failures have the claimed shape: one node stuck 3 to 34 heights behind, holding everything for its height except one decisive message.
- **V1 (6 cases):** round 0, precommit step, with the proposal, all 4 prevotes and 2 of the 3 precommits needed.
- **V2 (10 cases):** round 1 after timeouts, with 3 prevotes and 3 precommits for the decided block but no proposal.

Usually the other three then stall at height 7 with 5 validators and 399 power, as reported. When node 0 (the payer) is the stuck one, payments name stale block ids. No node ever admits the newcomer and the rest keep committing (heights 14-36), which matches the investigator's "most dumps" wording and their trace -085135. The investigator's own V1 trace (-965626) and height-1 V2 trace (-054378) show the drops they claim. Three of my V2 cases are node 3 at height 1-2 and have no drop log; at height 1 the proposal may also have arrived before evStart (onProposal drops it while heightVals is nil). The fix's own comment names that path, and the fix covers it.

**Mechanism, at unit level:**
- On 35b4e7f a re-gossip tick during the next height carries 3 precommits and 0 proposals. It rescues V1 but never V2.
- After a commit, 35b4e7f sends nothing.
- With the fix, both the commit-time send and the tick rescue both states.
- Code reading confirms the rest. commit() resets heightProposals, reGossipProposal sends only the current round, relay fires only on first receipt at the current height, and chaosNet has no Peers() or checkpoint source.

**Regression test (check 2):** it passes 3/3 with the fix. It fails 3/3 at window_test.go:254 with node.go reverted, and 3/3 with either half of the fix removed.

**Code review (check 3):**
- The diff touches only node/node.go (+19/-6) and node/window_test.go (pure addition). chaos_test.go is unchanged, so no assertion is weakened. The existing count-based tests are unaffected: votes_test.go takes its baseline after h.commit, and the proposal_relay tests never cross a commit.
- Nothing changes in signing (SignProposal, VerifyProposal, SignVote), ledger digests, persistence (Checkpoint, sign log), or the Message wire types. lastProposal lives only in memory, and its guard (Height > 0 and equal to lastCommit.Height) also filters a stale value after fastForward or a restart.
- Safety is unchanged: only messages signed by their authors are re-sent, and every check applies on receipt. Evidence.Valid compares digests before signatures, so nodes already past the height drop the re-sent precommits cheaply.
- The fix is minimal: about 10 net code lines, reusing the 9697404 loop. gofmt and go vet are clean, including -C ui.

**Suites (check 4):** both pass twice; see the rates table.

**Housekeeping:**
- I did not modify or push any worktree or branch. The investigator's worktree is clean at 631a8d5 with no upstream.
- post-emudhra-phase1 moved from f894ffe to cd8229e during my runs. The new commits touch only review docs, so the baseline still holds.
- The investigator's "No Go 1.27 effect" claim was not re-measured; I ran only go1.27.3, as the task asked.

problems.detail: Overlapping fixes on sibling branches edit the same node.go lines. chaos-admission 631a8d5 (gossipLastCommit) is functionally the same change: it keeps the decided proposal and sends it with the last commit at commit and on re-gossip. chaos-equivocator 01f0f34 is a subset that sends only the precommits at commit. Merging more than one will conflict, so take one (lossdup's or admission's) and drop the rest. This is not a defect of this fix.

The stranding split differs from the report's 5/5. In my 19 diagnosed base strandings, 15 lacked the round-0 proposal while holding the 3 round-0 precommits, and 4 held the proposal with only 2 precommits. In 3 of the 15, the node held the decided block as its own round-1 proposal (same digest) plus the round-0 quorum, and still could not decide, because the driver needs the proposal of the precommit round. The 4 one-short nodes sat in round 0 with no timer armed, which contradicts the report's line that timers kept moving them to new rounds. Neither point changes the conclusion: the fix covers both classes.

Cost: every node re-broadcasts the full decided block at every commit and on every re-gossip tick, even when no node is behind. That roughly doubles block traffic per height; the investigator disclosed this. The two parts serve different cases. The send at commit is what fixes the chaos test (tick-only strands 8/60, commit-only 0/60). The tick send of the proposal is what rescues the dead-bootstrap halt repro (commit-only halts 3/3). Both are justified, and the code (7 non-comment lines) is minimal for that.

verifications.notes:
Verdict: the root cause and the fix hold up.

1. Failure rates (go1.27.3, -race, GOLEDGER_CHAOS_SLACK=4, ABBA batches of 10, uptime logged per batch):
- Exact committed test: before 5/220, after 0/220.
- Instrumented copy: before 2/220, after 0/220.
- Combined: 7/440 against 0/440, one-sided Fisher p = 0.008.
- Stranding is the strong signal: 20/220 against 0/220 instrumented (p = 6e-7). With the diagnostic runs added, 39/360 against 0/290.
- Every failure was 'no payment landed' with node 0 stranded early. No data race and no panic appeared.

2. Root cause, checked independently. A diagnostic copy of the scenario classifies each stranded node's held state after Stop. Every one of 19 base strandings (8 more at 25-30% loss) lacked part of the decided round's certificate: the round's proposal, or one of its precommits. No stranded node held a same-round proposal and a precommit quorum without deciding, so I found nothing pointing to a different bug.
- The code path matches the report. reGossipProposal sends only the current round at the current height. Late precommits are relayed only by nodes at that height. Base re-gossip sent lastCommit.Votes but never the proposal, and only on the tick.
- chaosNet has no catch-up source (no Bootstrap, no Peers()). catchUpSources returns only Bootstrap when it is set.
- Unstranded runs made at least 20 blocks in 4 s before the fix and at least 24 after, against the test's floor of 6. The threshold is not too strict, and the test is unchanged.

3. Regression test. TestTheLastCommitCarriesItsProposal fails on the full revert at re-gossip:false. A copy that runs only the re-gossip case fails at re-gossip:true. Partial reverts:
- No send at commit: fails.
- Commit sends only the proposal: fails.
- Tick send without the proposal: fails the re-gossip case.
- No proposal anywhere: fails both cases.
With the fix it passes 50/50 under -race, with no timers involved.

4. Wire and storage: the diff is node/node.go plus one added test only. The signing fields, the ledger digest, Message/ProposalMsg, the Checkpoint JSON and the sign-log JSON are untouched. lastProposal is unexported and never serialized. Its guard (height > 0 and equal to lastCommit's height) never sends a zero or stale proposal, including after fastForward or a restart.
- Identical late precommits are rejected in Evidence.Valid before any signature check, so the extra sends are cheap for nodes past the height.

5. Suites and checks: gofmt -l . prints nothing. go vet passes in the root module and in ui. Both suites pass twice.

6. Side claims:
- GODEBUG=asynctimerchan=1 is fatal at startup on go1.27.3, for both the go command and the test binary.
- The investigator's logs match their counts: 3/400 failed and 45/400 stranded before, 0 after.
- I did not re-measure the go1.26.4 configurations.

Other observations:
- post-emudhra-phase1 moved during my run, to f29b1d6, which touches review docs only. I modified no worktree or branch.
- Optional hardening: the guard could also check p.Block.StateDigest == lastCommit.BlockDigest. In practice the first-wins rule already makes them equal.

problems.detail: 01f0f34 makes R1 much rarer but does not eliminate it. With both fixes, R1 occurred 3 times in 1,320 runs at 30% loss (seeds 1793124109922520402, 1793124508556330605, 1793124919492074418): a straggler stayed at h2 with byz counted out, lacking one honest precommit, while the others went on to h76-h84. In the two runs with commit history, all three deciders committed h2 with all four honest precommits, so each sent the missing vote at decide time. All three sends, plus the original send and its relays, were lost, and the others passed h3 before the next 400 ms re-gossip. The decide-time send is one more lossy broadcast, so the residual is roughly loss^3 times the old R1 rate. It is not the guarantee in the 01f0f34 commit message ('A node still at that height gets them before the others can finish the next height'), and the report's 'R1 9/300 -> 0/300' is a sampling result. Here R1 went from 5/300 (base) to 3/1320 (fixed), p=0.007. No residual appeared at the shipped 10% loss (0/2020), where it should be negligible. The commit message and report should say the fix mitigates R1. Fully closing it needs catch-up in chaosNet or re-gossip of older commits, which is the owner's call.

R2' (not fixed, as the investigator said) is broader than described and is the main remaining failure under heavy loss: 7 of 1,020 fixed-tree runs at 30%, and 0 of 2,020 at 10%. Besides a fourth honest node precommitting nil, it includes a fourth node that never precommitted in the decided round. In seed 1793124748212570441 it left round 0 on the precommit timeout, which the double-signer's first precommit had armed by briefly making 2/3-any. In seed 1793125062321588429 it lacked one honest prevote, so it had no polka. At the slashing height R2' does not halt the network: the others continue and only that node is left behind (seeds 1793124489972479512, 1793125062321588429).

docs/consensus.md was not updated for the new driver rule. Its Precommit bullet ('On ⅔ precommits for a real digest it decides') does not mention that a node now precommits the decided block in a round where it has not precommitted. Its Equivocation section says 'a double-signer cannot help form a quorum'. That was already inaccurate before this fix: a double-signer's first-seen vote counts until its conflicting vote arrives, and R2 and R2' depend on exactly that.

The mix of modes at the shipped 10% loss differs from the report's emphasis. Of 4 instrumented base failures at 10%, 3 were R2 and 1 was R1; the report's only traced 10% failure was R1. The fix covers both, so this does not change the conclusion.

verifications.notes:
Verdict: the root cause is confirmed. The fix removes the flake at the shipped settings: base 6/2020 vs fix 0/2020 at 10% loss across two interleaved measurements, one-sided Fisher p=0.016. The investigator's 600 runs per side could not show this. The R2 half of the fix is complete. The R1 half only mitigates (see the major problem).

How I checked:
- Root cause. I reproduced R1 and R2 independently with a race-free state dump taken after Stop, and classified each failure from the nodes' votes and commit voters. R1: the straggler at h2 has byz counted out and lacks exactly one honest precommit, while the others are far ahead. R2: the decider's h(n) commit holds byz plus three honest votes and not its own; the other nodes hold 300 < 334. Both appeared at base at 10% and at 30%. The investigator's traces (diag-head R1, diag-c99 R2) match.
- The node and consensus code is identical between my base and 35b4e7f.
- Attribution, 30% loss, 300 runs each:
  - driver fix only: 4 failures, all R1; it removes R2 but not R1.
  - node fix only: 2 failures (1 R2', 1 left-behind straggler).
  - both fixes: 1 failure (R1 residual).
  - R2 never appeared with the driver fix: 0 in 4,640 runs across all fixed configs.
- Regression tests:
  - TestDriverPrecommitsTheBlockItDecides fails 6/6 with driver.go reverted and passes 200/200 with the fix.
  - TestDecidingNodeSendsTheCommitAtOnce fails 20/20 with node.go reverted and passes 200/200 with the fix.
  - Mutation: with sendLastCommit removed from reGossipVotes, the existing TestReGossipCarriesTheLastCommitToANodeStillAtThatHeight fails 5/5 while the new test passes, so both send paths stay covered.
- Check (3):
  - Only tests were added; no existing assertion changed.
  - Nothing in signing/, ledger/, persist.go, messages.go, vote.go or commit.go changed, so no preimage, digest, struct or JSON format changed.
  - The decide-time precommit goes through castVote and logVote. logVote signs the round's proposal into Locked when it is not yet held.
  - The change is minimal: a 4-line branch, plus one extracted function and one call.
- Safety. The new precommit is for the already-decided value, in a round the node never precommitted in. The first such vote can only follow a quorum whose honest members precommitted after a polka (more than 1/3 of power locked), so it can complete no conflicting quorum. No FORK, SUPPLY or DATA RACE in about 6,300 chaos runs.
- Suites on the fixed tree, load about 3-4:

  - GOLEDGER_CHAOS_SLACK=4 go test -race -count=1 ./... passed twice (36 s; node 34.4 s and 34.9 s).
  - go test -C ui -race -count=1 ./... passed twice (22.7 s each).
